text: Edson Barboza vs. Drakkar Klose: Reliving MMA's Most Violent Finish & The Aftermath Edson Barboza vs. Drakkar Klose: A Fight Etched in MMA History The world of Mixed Martial Arts (MMA) is filled with unforgettable moments – spectacular knockouts, dramatic submissions, and battles of attrition that test the limits of human endurance. Among these, the fight between Edson Barboza and Drakkar Klose at UFC Fight Night: Waterson vs. Hill on October 3, 2020, stands out, not just for its explosive finish, but for the circumstances surrounding it and the lasting impact it had on both athletes. However, Barboza had also faced adversity, experiencing losses against top-tier opponents like Khabib Nurmagomedov, Tony Ferguson, and Justin Gaethje. These defeats, while highlighting areas for improvement, also showcased his resilience and willingness to learn and evolve. Drakkar Klose: The Rising Contender In contrast to Barboza's veteran status, Drakkar Klose entered the fight as a rising contender looking to establish himself in the competitive lightweight division. Known for his wrestling background and a relentless pressure fighting style, Klose presented a different challenge. He was a tough, determined fighter with a penchant for grinding out victories. Prior to facing Barboza, Klose had accumulated a solid record, including wins over Lando Vannata and Bobby Green. His strengths included: - Strong wrestling skills, allowing him to control opponents and dictate the pace of the fight. - A relentless pressure style, constantly pushing forward and engaging his opponents. - Good durability and cardio, enabling him to maintain a high level of activity throughout the fight. Klose aimed to use his wrestling and pressure to nullify Barboza's striking and impose his will on the fight. He saw the Barboza fight as an opportunity to elevate his status and move closer to title contention. The Buildup: Tensions and Expectations The pre-fight narrative was compelling. It was a classic striker vs. grappler matchup, with Barboza's explosive striking pitted against Klose's wrestling and pressure. The stylistic contrast fueled anticipation among fans and analysts alike. Klose, known for his confidence and occasionally brash demeanor, made it clear that he intended to test Barboza's wrestling and wear him down. He predicted a victory, emphasizing his belief that he could neutralize Barboza's striking and impose his grappling game. Barboza, as always, remained focused and respectful, acknowledging Klose's skills but expressing confidence in his own abilities. He emphasized his striking and his commitment to improving his overall game. He knew that Klose would attempt to take him down, and he prepared accordingly. The stage was set for a clash of styles, with both fighters determined to prove themselves and advance their careers. The fight was expected to be a closely contested battle, with the outcome hinging on who could successfully implement their game plan. Round One: A Tactical Dance The fight began with both fighters feeling each other out, establishing their range and testing their opponent's reactions. Barboza, as expected, looked to control the distance with his kicks, while Klose sought opportunities to close the gap and initiate grappling exchanges. Barboza landed several of his signature leg kicks, immediately targeting Klose's lead leg. These kicks were designed to slow Klose down and limit his mobility, making it more difficult for him to close the distance and initiate takedowns. Klose, however, was persistent in his pursuit of takedowns. He managed to secure a couple of takedowns in the first round, briefly controlling Barboza on the ground. While Barboza was able to quickly get back to his feet, Klose's success in securing takedowns demonstrated his commitment to his game plan. The round was competitive, with both fighters having their moments of success. Barboza's striking was sharp and effective, while Klose's wrestling posed a threat. At the end of the round, it was unclear who had the advantage. The Knockout: A Moment of Brutal Precision The second round began with a similar dynamic. Barboza continued to utilize his striking, while Klose pressed forward, looking for opportunities to grapple. However, what happened next would forever be etched in MMA history. As Klose moved forward, Barboza unleashed a perfectly timed and devastating right uppercut. The punch landed flush on Klose's chin, immediately shutting off his lights. Klose crumpled to the canvas, unconscious, in one of the most violent knockouts the sport has ever witnessed. The entire sequence, from the initial exchange to the final blow, was a blur of speed and precision. The crowd erupted in a mixture of shock and awe. Barboza had delivered a knockout for the ages, showcasing his incredible striking power and timing. It was a highlight-reel finish that would be replayed countless times. The knockout wasn't just a result of power; it was a testament to Barboza's technical skill and his ability to read his opponent. He recognized Klose's forward pressure and anticipated his movement, allowing him to perfectly time the uppercut. The Aftermath: Controversy and Lasting Effects The immediate aftermath of the knockout was one of celebration for Barboza and concern for Klose. Barboza had secured a spectacular victory and re-established himself as a force to be reckoned with in the lightweight division. Klose, on the other hand, was knocked out cold and required medical attention. However, the story didn't end there. In the weeks and months following the fight, a controversy emerged regarding the circumstances surrounding the bout. Drakkar Klose claimed that he had suffered a neck injury during a pre-fight face-off with Barboza at the weigh-ins. He alleged that Barboza had pushed him, causing him to tense up his neck and suffer spasms. Klose further claimed that the neck injury severely hampered his ability to prepare for the fight and ultimately contributed to his loss. He argued that he wasn't at 100% going into the fight and that the injury significantly impacted his performance. Klose also claimed he experienced concussion symptoms and further aggravated his condition during the fight. Regardless of the circumstances, Klose's health became a major concern. He was sidelined for an extended period due to the neck injury and concussion symptoms. His career was put on hold as he focused on his recovery. The injury not only affected his physical well-being but also took a toll on his mental state. He expressed frustration and disappointment over the injury, which he felt had derailed his career momentum. Following the Klose fight, Barboza continued to compete at a high level, facing a series of tough opponents. He eventually moved down to the featherweight division, seeking a fresh challenge and an opportunity to compete against new contenders. In response to these concerns, some MMA organizations have implemented stricter guidelines regarding face-off procedures. These guidelines aim to minimize the risk of physical contact and ensure the safety of the fighters. Some organizations have prohibited fighters from touching each other during face-offs, while others have implemented stricter supervision and monitoring to prevent any potential incidents. The goal is to strike a balance between promoting the fight and protecting the well-being of the athletes. Lessons Learned: Risk Management and Athlete Safety The Barboza-Klose fight serves as a reminder of the inherent risks associated with MMA. It highlights the importance of athlete safety and the need for comprehensive risk management strategies. MMA organizations have a responsibility to ensure that fighters are adequately protected from unnecessary harm. This includes implementing strict medical protocols, providing comprehensive pre-fight medical evaluations, and ensuring that fighters are fully recovered from any injuries before returning to competition. Fighters also have a responsibility to prioritize their own health and safety. They should be transparent about any injuries they may have sustained and seek appropriate medical attention when necessary. They should also be willing to withdraw from a fight if they are not fully fit to compete. Conclusion: A Fight That Resonates The fight between Edson Barboza and Drakkar Klose remains a significant moment in MMA history. It was a fight that featured a spectacular knockout, a controversial aftermath, and lasting implications for both fighters involved. The fight serves as a testament to the unpredictable nature of combat sports and the importance of athlete safety. While Barboza continued his career at a high level, showcasing his striking prowess, Klose faced a long and challenging recovery process. The controversy surrounding the fight sparked a debate about pre-fight face-offs and the need for stricter safety protocols. Ultimately, the Barboza-Klose fight is a reminder of the physical and mental toll that MMA can take on athletes. It underscores the importance of prioritizing athlete safety and implementing comprehensive risk management strategies to protect the well-being of the fighters. The legacy of this fight lives on, reminding fans and fighters alike of the explosive potential, the inherent risks, and the complex dynamics that make MMA one of the most captivating and compelling sports in the world. title: UFC 319 Predictions: Odds, Card Breakdown, and Best Bets for Saturday, August 16
text: Live from the United Center in Chicago, IL, we have an amazing card at UFC 319. The Middleweight title is on the line as current champ Dricus Du Plessis takes on undefeated challenger Khamzat Chimaev. We also have a ton of other fights lining this entire card. Today, I will break down my 3 favorite bets for this weekend’s fight card. Let’s get into it! This should be a fun fight against two pretty high-level guys early in the card. Barboza is one of the greatest strikers to ever grace the UFC Octagon. He has a career UFC record of 18-12 with 8 KO/TKOs in that span. He now takes on Drakkar Klose, who is 9-3 in his UFC career, but is coming off a brutal KO loss back in December. Klose is a very strong and explosive fighter, but he will have a tough time cracking the striking ability of Barboza. Both of these guys are pretty old, Barboza at 39 and Klose at 37, but they still have some fight left in the tank. I think Barboza and his legendary kicks will give him this fight. I think he will manage the distance well and capitalize when Klose needs to close the distance. MY PICK: Edson Barboza -140 I cannot wait for this fight. Aaron Pico is making his highly anticipated UFC debut against one of the UFC’s hottest prospects, Lerone Murphy. Both of these guys are extremely explosive and could be potential challengers in the lightweight division. This fight comes with a ton of question marks, though. The last Bellator phenom we saw in the UFC, Patchy Mix, got dismantled. So, can Pico change the tune? I think Pico needs to lean on his wrestling background in this fight. He was a junior world freestyle champion and the number one recruit in the nation before foregoing college and fighting full-time. Murphy is a very dangerous striker, and while Pico is also skilled in his striking game, he needs to play to his strengths. Give me Pico to give Murphy his first career loss this weekend, but in a close decision. MY PICK: Aaron Pico +140 Here. We. Go. The Middleweight title is on the line as current champ DDP takes on terrifying challenger Khamzat Chimaev. This fight is guaranteed to be fireworks, as Chimaev is known for his high-paced attacking, and DDP is known for his unorthodox, but brutal, style of fighting. DDP’s last loss as a pro was all the way back in 2018, and since then, he has beaten everyone in his path, including Israel Adesanya, Robert Whittaker, and Sean Strickland. Chimaev has never lost, and his 2 latest wins were against former champions Robert Whittaker and Kamaru Usman. He has proven he is legit in every way, and now he finally gets his title shot. Chimaev is a big favorite in this one, sitting at -258 at the time of me writing this. DDP is as tough as they come, and his unorthodox style of striking has given people tons of problems. The issue with that is Khamzat won’t be looking to stand for too long. Chimaev has an average control time of 55.2% in his UFC career, meaning he is in a dominant position in grappling more than half the time he's fought in the UFC. I love DDP, and I think he has a chance here, but I’m not sure he will be able to handle the onslaught of Khamzat. I think Khamzat takes his back and ends it pretty early. MY PICK: Khamzat Chimaev by Submission +130

text: Khamzat Chimaev is ready to take over the UFC. He will first have to get past the crafty Dricus du Plessis, who defends his middleweight title at UFC 319 on August 16 inside the United Center. du Plessis (23-2) became the first South African to become UFC champion. Winner of eleven straight fights, the former kickboxing star has beaten three former champions. He has learned to adapt in every fight with his unique offense. The fight is a long time coming for Chimaev (14-0), who recently broke the jaw of Robert Whittaker. One of the most dangerous fighters in MMA, the Chechen had a rocket ship strapped to his back early, and a win could propel him to superstardom. UFC 319 will also see the octagon debut of Aaron Pico and the returns of Michael Page and Kai Asakura. Jessica Andrade once again competes this year, as does the surging Chase Hooper. With the help of the FanDuel Sportsbook, The Sporting News makes predictions on the entire card at UFC 319. Chimaev was destined for superstardom since his UFC debut, before a COVID-19 infection affected his career. Still, he’s a killer, using ground and pound to decimate the opposition. du Plessis has only been taken down three times in the UFC and is one of the most unorthodox fighters in MMA history. Just ask Israel Adesanya and Sean Strickland. MORE: How to bet on combat sports While not a serious factor, “DDP” is known for playing mind games. If he gets into Chimaev’s head and forces him to make mistakes, du Plessis can take advantage. One thing against the champion is that he’s offensively open, which Chimaev can easily take advantage of. For Chimaev, does he have a lengthy gas tank after the first round, especially against someone like du Plessis? If Chimaev can grapple early, he should finish the fight in the first round. If it goes past the first? du Plessis will force him to work and slip by a few grappling attempts. Dricus may not knock him out, but he could give Chimaev trouble if his cardio is on point. While this transition deserves deeper discussion, we’ll save that for another time. The main event features a thrilling middleweight title clash between champion Dricus Du Plessis of South Africa and the No. 3-ranked Khamzat Chimaev, a Russian grappler widely regarded as one of the UFC’s most dangerous fighters. The fight card begins with early prelims at 3:00 p.m. PT, regular prelims at 5:00 p.m. PT, and the PPV portion at 7:00 p.m. PT. UFC 319 features 13 scheduled bouts, with five involving fighters at 170 pounds or heavier, offering a higher likelihood of finishes. Five matchups have a youth advantage of six years or more, and two bouts pit fighters aged 37 or older against each other—call them the “geriatric” battles! Last week’s parlay loss dropped my column’s record to 16-18, -0.47 units for the year. Let’s get back in the black with UFC 319! Khamzat Chimaev (-230) vs. Dricus Du Plessis (+195) Middleweight Championship (185 pounds) Main Event Khamzat Chimaev, a brown belt in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu (BJJ) with exceptional wrestling, trains between Sweden and the UAE. He burst onto the UFC scene like a lightning bolt, dominating opponents across welterweight and middleweight with devastating finishes. However, recent health issues, inactivity, and a lack of elite middleweight competition have tempered his momentum. His notable middleweight wins include a one-sided thrashing of former champion Robert Whittaker last October, a close majority decision over welterweight Kamaru Usman (who took the fight on short notice), and a favorable matchup against Kevin Holland. Chimaev’s aggressive, smothering style shines in the first two rounds, but he’s shown signs of fatigue against smaller opponents like Gilbert Burns and Usman. This vulnerability could be critical against a true middleweight like Du Plessis. A massive, dynamically strong middleweight with excellent cardio and durability, he’s not nimble or precise with his striking but thrives in chaotic, pressure-heavy brawls. title: Drakkar Klose Does Not Want To Have Any Regrets
text: In January of 2017, Drakkar Klose stepped into the UFC Octagon for the first time and improved his unbeaten pro MMA record to 7-0-1 with a decision win over Devin Powell. Nearly nine years later, the native of Kalamazoo, Michigan, is still here, still doing his thing at the highest level of the sport, and as he approaches his UFC 319 bout against Edson Barboza this weekend, he still believes he’s got something left in the tank. “Yeah, I’m not on empty,” Klose laughs. “I probably got a half a tank left.” UFC Coming To Paramount In 2026! Read The Announcement That’s enough to get him somewhere in a notoriously tough lightweight division, and he knows it. He just needs to have everything come together on Saturday, and a big win over a well-respected veteran like Barboza will do wonders for his future. “I hope so, and I believe it will,” he said. “Last fight I trained hard, but right before the walkout I started thinking about my brother and I started crying a little bit. I did everything right, but I wasn't mentally prepared for that fight. I was talking to (UFC Hall of Famer) Mark Kerr and he was talking to me about when he had lost his mom and how he was angry and all that, and he was like, ‘You're never going to get over the pain; you’ve just got to learn how to live with it. It's been a year now, and I've just been trying to learn to live with it and cherish the moments that I did have with my brother. So I'm in a way better head space than I was that last fight.” That last fight, a first-round knockout loss at the hands of Joel Alvarez, came just four months after the senseless murder of Klose’s brother, Tuan Williams. Remarkably, Klose made it to the fight in Tampa in December, but he wasn’t ready. It’s the part of the fight game many don’t understand, that for all the superhuman things athletes do in the Octagon, they’re still human, and sometimes what happens outside of competition affects what happens in it. Klose got a reminder of that in June when he went to New Jersey to watch his teammate Sean O’Malley attempt to regain his bantamweight title against Merab Dvalishvili and heard what some fans had to say. MORE UFC 319: UFC 319 Embedded | Fight by Fight Preview | Fighters On The Rise | Significant Stats | Matchup Spotlight: Neal vs Prates “Just sitting in the stands, you hear all this crazy stuff out of people's mouth and it's like, we're human. We're just like you, but we just chose to fight. And I think some people, they just don't understand that.” Some won’t ever get it, but it doesn’t stop people like Klose from trying to block out the noise and go to work. And he’s done that leading up to his meeting with Barboza, a longtime lightweight contender returning to the division after an eight-fight stint at 145 pounds. “He's definitely a dangerous opponent and he's been doing it for a long time,” said Klose of the Brazilian. “He's fought the who's who of MMA, and he has a good showing with them. But what his downfall is, it's his wrestling. He fought at ’55 and the guys were taking him down, wrestling him up, and then he made that transition down to ‘45. He had some success down there, but when guys started wrestling with him, it was the same thing that it was at ‘55. And he is a little bit older now and, to be honest, I don't think he has too many more left in him, so I think he's just trying to fight where he's comfortable. He's not cutting that much weight, but he's always a dangerous opponent and that excites me.” The 37-year-old Klose also doesn’t mind being the young guy in the matchup against his 39-year-old opponent. FOLLOW @UFCNEWS: On Facebook | On Instagram | On X | On Threads “Two years younger, but hey, I’ll take it,” he laughs. “When they first gave me the call, I was like, thank God, it's someone older than me, because we all like to think that we still have it, but I'm not going to lie, I've slowed down throughout the years. It's kind of hard to compete with these younger guys, and good thing I have these younger guys to still compete with to show me like, ‘Hey man, this is a young man's sport.’ (Laughs) I'm just glad I get to go in there and compete with someone a little bit older than me.” Older, yes. Wiser, yes again. And though Klose knows he is closer to the end of his career than he was back in 2017, he believes he still has plenty to give to his fans and the sport. “I'm not going to sit here and lie,” he admits. “I always wanted to chase the belt, but it just feels like it's not in my cards. So, for me right now, I want to go out, try to make as much money as I can for my family, and when it's my time, walk away on top, hopefully with a great record and still having my brain cells intact.” For most, that might be a tough conversation to have. It wasn’t for Klose, one of the sport’s class acts. Order UFC 319: Du Plessis vs Chimaev “I always had a lot of regrets in wrestling,” he said. “Like, man, I wish I'd have done this. And then I found MMA and I was able to put all those, ‘oh, I wish I would've done this’ things and apply that to my MMA career. So put everything into it, and when it is time for me to walk away, I won't have those ‘I wish I would’ve done this,’ thoughts.” He shouldn’t, because more than eight years on the UFC roster, with nine wins and counting, isn’t anything to scoff at. And he’s still going, so the best may be yet to come. “I’ve lived with a lot of injuries along the road, but I grew as a person and that's all life is about,” said Klose of his run in the big show. “If you don't grow, why are you living? I still have friends who are like, ‘Oh, you changed.’ I'm like, yes, I changed. That's what you're supposed to do in life. If you're the same person you were from day one, you didn't learn anything in life.” Don't miss a moment of UFC 319: Du Plessis vs Chimaev, live from United Center in Chicago, Illinois on August 16, 2025. title: Edson Barbosa vs. Drakkar Klose
text: The first thing people are going to do here is point out that Barbosa is 39 while completely ignoring the fact that Drakkar is 37 and has a liteny of injuries. I don't think age will be a factor here but pace might be. Edson cuts a ton of weight and does tend to slow down. If Drakkar comes out with a wrestle heavy gameplan he could definitely wear on Edson and take away the power. I'm split here because I really want to pick Drakkar as a dog, but I haven't really seen anything yet that tells me Barboza is washed. I'm going to slightly lean Edson here but might change that pick as we get closer to the fight. Edson Barbosa Edson Barbosa is a great striker with amazing movement. He has fought every single person in this division and is a walking highlight reel of KOs and submissions. He is unbelievably fast and insanely technical. Barboza doesn't initiate many takedowns, but he is very good on the ground with some sneaky submissions. He is coming off the main event loss to Lerone Murphy more than a year ago. Drakkar Klose Drakkar Klose is a very good wrestler who developed striking as well. He was a state champion wrestler who uses his wrestling offense, but does have some issues defending takedowns. He has solid boxing with power and speed. Overall he is a well rounded guy who can go the distance or finish a fight. He is coming off KO loss to Joel Alvarez where he had a takedown but couldn't hang in the striking.

title: UFC 319 staff picks including Dricus du Plessis predicted to end Khamzat Chimaev's undefeated streak
text: The experts have made their picks, and there are some interesting predictions for UFC 319. The event is the biggest UFC show for a while, featuring a massive UFC Middleweight title clash between Dricus du Plessis and the undefeated challenger, Khamzat Chimaev. Both men have yet to lose in the UFC, building up some impressive winning streaks en route to UFC 319. Du Plessis and Chimaev top an impressive-looking card, which also sees Lerone Murphy and Aaron Pico battle in the co-main event, as well as an action-packed undercard and prelims. The Bloody Elbow staff has made their predictions about what will happen at UFC 319, including the two main event fights as well as the Fight of the Night and Performance of the Night bonus winners Dricus du Plessis vs Khamzat Chimaev prediction - Harvey Leonard: Dricus du Plessis - Jordan Ellis: Khamzat Chimaev - Ross Markey: Dricus du Plessis The Bloody Elbow experts have made a split decision on who will win the UFC 319 main event, which could be how du Plessis retains his title, given how close this fight could be. The main event features two fighters who are undefeated in the UFC, with du Plessis’s last defeat coming via knockout before he made his debut in the promotion. His 9-0 record since his 2020 debut has helped position du Plessis as the #4 pound-for-pound fighter in the company. Wins over Sean Strickland and Israel Adesanya saw him win and defend the UFC Middleweight title in impressive fashion. Both Harvey and Ross can’t look past a du Plessis victory, but Jordan is backing the undefeated Chechen Chimaev to use his size advantage to take out the champion and claim his Middleweight crown. Lerone Murphy vs Aaron Pico prediction - Harvey Leonard: Lerone Murphy - Jordan Ellis: Aaron Pico - Ross Markey: Lerone Murphy Aaron Pico makes the jump over to the UFC after a good career in Bellator, but he will have to contend with an undefeated opponent who will be the clear favorite for this bout. Pico takes on Lerone Murphy in the UFC 319 main event, bringing his famous knockout blows to the biggest promotion, and Jordan thinks he has enough to finish Murphy on August 16. He won three of his last five fights via KO, with his only loss since 2019 coming due to a shoulder injury suffered at the end of the first round against Jeremy Kennedy. However, Pico hasn’t competed since February last year, and that ring rust could give Murphy more of a chance to win. Harvey and Ross are backing the 16-0-1 UFC star to beat the debuting Pico, who a UFC legend questioned why he took such a hard fight for his maiden voyage in the promotion. A loss here could derail his MMA career despite huge future promise, which seems likely if Murphy is in top form once again. UFC 319 Fight of the Night prediction - Harvey Leonard: Edson Barboza vs. Drakker Klose - Jordan Ellis: Geoff Neal vs Carlos Prates - Ross Markey: Edson Barboza vs. Drakker Klose Harvey and Ross are once again in agreement, choosing the Edson Barboza and Drakkar Klose fight as the one that will earn a $50,000 bonus at the end of the night at UFC 319. Barboza continues into his 17th year in MMA, shockingly moving up to Lightweight following his spirited defeat to Lerone Murphy back in May, pushing the undefeated fighter to the limit over five rounds. While his record isn’t the best over the past few years, nobody could ever accuse Barboza of not giving his all or putting on great fights. That is why his bout with Klose could win the bonus, with both men coming off the back of losses, with knockout power in their gloves, and with something to prove at UFC 319. Meanwhile, Jordan is excited by one of the most high-profile bouts outside of the main event, as Carlos Prates battles Geoff Neal in a Welterweight battle. The fight was originally scheduled for UFC 314 before Neal pulled out of the bout and the pair could cause chaos on August 16. Both men are prone to finishes in their fights, whether on the giving or receiving end, leaving either vulnerable for a spectacular knockout shot or a brutal submission in the middle of the octagon, in a fight that you won’t be able to take your eyes off of. UFC 319 Performance of the Night prediction - Harvey Leonard: Kai Asakura - Jordan Ellis: Michael Page - Ross Markey: Carlos Prates There are three distinct picks for the Performance of the Night winner, with all three fighters having a good claim to earn the $50,000 bonus. Harvey is backing Japanese star Kai Asakura to impress in his first fight of the year, following 2024’s submission defeat to Alexandre Pantoja at UFC 310. This is just his second fight in the UFC, after numerous impressive bouts in his home country for Rizin before making the jump to the United States. Asakura will want to make a splash when he faces Tim Elliot at UFC 319. Meanwhile, Jordan is backing Michael “Venom” Page to continue his rehab in the octagon after his UFC 303 loss to Ian Machado Garry. He impressed in his return to Middleweight against Sharabudin Magomedov in February, and will look to use some more of his famed knockout power to finish Jared Cannonier at UFC 319. Finally, Ross can’t look past Prates for the Performance of the Night winner. With the ability to finish a fight at any time, Prates is in pole position to pick up the bonus if he can beat Neal on August 16.

title: Drakkar Klose Does Not Want To Have Any Regrets
text: In January of 2017, Drakkar Klose stepped into the UFC Octagon for the first time and improved his unbeaten pro MMA record to 7-0-1 with a decision win over Devin Powell. Nearly nine years later, the native of Kalamazoo, Michigan, is still here, still doing his thing at the highest level of the sport, and as he approaches his UFC 319 bout against Edson Barboza this weekend, he still believes he’s got something left in the tank. “Yeah, I’m not on empty,” Klose laughs. “I probably got a half a tank left.” UFC Coming To Paramount In 2026! Read The Announcement That’s enough to get him somewhere in a notoriously tough lightweight division, and he knows it. He just needs to have everything come together on Saturday, and a big win over a well-respected veteran like Barboza will do wonders for his future. “I hope so, and I believe it will,” he said. “Last fight I trained hard, but right before the walkout I started thinking about my brother and I started crying a little bit. I did everything right, but I wasn't mentally prepared for that fight. I was talking to (UFC Hall of Famer) Mark Kerr and he was talking to me about when he had lost his mom and how he was angry and all that, and he was like, ‘You're never going to get over the pain; you’ve just got to learn how to live with it. It's been a year now, and I've just been trying to learn to live with it and cherish the moments that I did have with my brother. So I'm in a way better head space than I was that last fight.” That last fight, a first-round knockout loss at the hands of Joel Alvarez, came just four months after the senseless murder of Klose’s brother, Tuan Williams. Remarkably, Klose made it to the fight in Tampa in December, but he wasn’t ready. It’s the part of the fight game many don’t understand, that for all the superhuman things athletes do in the Octagon, they’re still human, and sometimes what happens outside of competition affects what happens in it. Klose got a reminder of that in June when he went to New Jersey to watch his teammate Sean O’Malley attempt to regain his bantamweight title against Merab Dvalishvili and heard what some fans had to say. MORE UFC 319: UFC 319 Embedded | Fight by Fight Preview | Fighters On The Rise | Significant Stats | Matchup Spotlight: Neal vs Prates “Just sitting in the stands, you hear all this crazy stuff out of people's mouth and it's like, we're human. We're just like you, but we just chose to fight. And I think some people, they just don't understand that.” Some won’t ever get it, but it doesn’t stop people like Klose from trying to block out the noise and go to work. And he’s done that leading up to his meeting with Barboza, a longtime lightweight contender returning to the division after an eight-fight stint at 145 pounds. “He's definitely a dangerous opponent and he's been doing it for a long time,” said Klose of the Brazilian. “He's fought the who's who of MMA, and he has a good showing with them. But what his downfall is, it's his wrestling. He fought at ’55 and the guys were taking him down, wrestling him up, and then he made that transition down to ‘45. He had some success down there, but when guys started wrestling with him, it was the same thing that it was at ‘55. And he is a little bit older now and, to be honest, I don't think he has too many more left in him, so I think he's just trying to fight where he's comfortable. He's not cutting that much weight, but he's always a dangerous opponent and that excites me.” The 37-year-old Klose also doesn’t mind being the young guy in the matchup against his 39-year-old opponent. FOLLOW @UFCNEWS: On Facebook | On Instagram | On X | On Threads “Two years younger, but hey, I’ll take it,” he laughs. “When they first gave me the call, I was like, thank God, it's someone older than me, because we all like to think that we still have it, but I'm not going to lie, I've slowed down throughout the years. It's kind of hard to compete with these younger guys, and good thing I have these younger guys to still compete with to show me like, ‘Hey man, this is a young man's sport.’ (Laughs) I'm just glad I get to go in there and compete with someone a little bit older than me.” Older, yes. Wiser, yes again. And though Klose knows he is closer to the end of his career than he was back in 2017, he believes he still has plenty to give to his fans and the sport. “I'm not going to sit here and lie,” he admits. “I always wanted to chase the belt, but it just feels like it's not in my cards. So, for me right now, I want to go out, try to make as much money as I can for my family, and when it's my time, walk away on top, hopefully with a great record and still having my brain cells intact.” For most, that might be a tough conversation to have. It wasn’t for Klose, one of the sport’s class acts. Order UFC 319: Du Plessis vs Chimaev “I always had a lot of regrets in wrestling,” he said. “Like, man, I wish I'd have done this. And then I found MMA and I was able to put all those, ‘oh, I wish I would've done this’ things and apply that to my MMA career. So put everything into it, and when it is time for me to walk away, I won't have those ‘I wish I would’ve done this,’ thoughts.” He shouldn’t, because more than eight years on the UFC roster, with nine wins and counting, isn’t anything to scoff at. And he’s still going, so the best may be yet to come. “I’ve lived with a lot of injuries along the road, but I grew as a person and that's all life is about,” said Klose of his run in the big show. “If you don't grow, why are you living? I still have friends who are like, ‘Oh, you changed.’ I'm like, yes, I changed. That's what you're supposed to do in life. If you're the same person you were from day one, you didn't learn anything in life.” Don't miss a moment of UFC 319: Du Plessis vs Chimaev, live from United Center in Chicago, Illinois on August 16, 2025. title: Edson Barbosa vs. Drakkar Klose
text: The first thing people are going to do here is point out that Barbosa is 39 while completely ignoring the fact that Drakkar is 37 and has a liteny of injuries. I don't think age will be a factor here but pace might be. Edson cuts a ton of weight and does tend to slow down. If Drakkar comes out with a wrestle heavy gameplan he could definitely wear on Edson and take away the power. I'm split here because I really want to pick Drakkar as a dog, but I haven't really seen anything yet that tells me Barboza is washed. I'm going to slightly lean Edson here but might change that pick as we get closer to the fight. Edson Barbosa Edson Barbosa is a great striker with amazing movement. He has fought every single person in this division and is a walking highlight reel of KOs and submissions. He is unbelievably fast and insanely technical. Barboza doesn't initiate many takedowns, but he is very good on the ground with some sneaky submissions. He is coming off the main event loss to Lerone Murphy more than a year ago. Drakkar Klose Drakkar Klose is a very good wrestler who developed striking as well. He was a state champion wrestler who uses his wrestling offense, but does have some issues defending takedowns. He has solid boxing with power and speed. Overall he is a well rounded guy who can go the distance or finish a fight. He is coming off KO loss to Joel Alvarez where he had a takedown but couldn't hang in the striking.
